comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026–2027 Nanobiology TER Articles 3–5 and 8 control course requirements; the September 2026 chart corroborates their 180 EC. Freshly checked 8 October 2026. English instruction replaces normalized NLD-only metadata, preserving raw NLD provenance and TU Delft/Erasmus University Rotterdam institutional participation. Year one comprises twelve positions totaling 60 EC, with the first formal permissible mixed practical pair NB1430 Molecular Biology Techniques A and NB1445 Biophysics Techniques B, 4 EC each. This is a representative programme assignment, not a free student choice or a prediction of an individual assignment. The alternative is NB1435 plus NB1440; the programme informs students before 1 February 2027 and changes require permission. Year two comprises fourteen required units totaling 60 EC. Current NB2430 Nanotechnology is 3 EC; Article 11.7 prints 4 EC for an older-cohort transition and does not override the current entrant table. Year three is an approved 30-EC minor, NB3000 Bachelor End Project 20 EC and four distinct 2.5-EC electives totaling 10 EC. The electives are the first four formal list entries: NB3015 A Primer in Neuroscience, NB3024 Advanced Math Topics, NB3026 Biomolecular Ultrasound and NB3014 Computational Neuroscience. Selection follows formal order independently of UCR fit; catalogue prerequisites, capacity, enrolment and actual octal availability remain conditions, so this is not an exact future timetable. Outside electives and self-composed minors require Board approval. BEP admission requires all 60 first-year EC plus at least 60 EC from years two and three combined; an approved programme supervisor is required. No alternative pair, minor content or embedded skills adds credits. UCR assessment on 10 October 2026 freshly retrieved the current adopted Appendix and visually inspected the second-/third-year and elective table (PDF p.6), with first-year and project clauses text-checked. The current required courses, representative assigned practical pair, neutral four electives and 180-EC total remain unchanged. Historical transition weights do not override the current entrant table.

alternatives.concept: Study cells, biomolecules, genetics and experimental biology through substantial mathematical and computational analysis, including neural-system applications supported by the selected external electives. Preserve explicit gaps in nanoscale physics and measurement rather than substituting general science for them.

alternatives.labelRationale: Six molecular/physiological biology courses, three neural courses and fourteen mathematical/computational courses implement a quantitative living-systems curriculum. The label does not imply full Nanobiology or nanophysics formation.

alternatives.concept: Retain molecular/laboratory biology, quantitative modelling and neural function while prioritising pharmacology, immunity, anatomical structure/function and mechanisms of disease instead of advanced algorithmic and neural-network specialisation.

alternatives.labelRationale: Four biomedical courses replace algorithmic, optimisation and deep-learning specialisation, yielding a substantial molecular-disease focus with retained quantitative biology; the label makes no nanomedical-device claim.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each direction. Algorithms, Advanced Algorithms, Neural Networks & Deep Learning and Optimisation are replaced by Pharmacology, Infection & Immunity, Functional Anatomy and Mechanisms of Disease. This shifts advanced study from computational implementations to biological mechanism and intervention, rather than varying labels or incidental examples.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All hard workbook gates passed: 24 unique courses / 180 EC, PPD in year one, at least six level-300 courses, formal prerequisites in earlier terms and exact six-term availability. Biology and programming foundations precede laboratory, biochemistry and algorithmic work. Calculus/matrix foundations precede numerical and linear-system methods; Algorithms precedes Advanced Algorithms in the computational alternative. Brain foundations precede Perception & Action. Introductory data methods precede advanced learning/image methods. The open curriculum permits specialised medical work in year two after biology foundations; advisory physiology/biochemistry progression was considered without inventing additional prerequisites.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete, coherent related programmes pass the course-content, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. The molecular/quantitative core and medical-research direction are supported by independent target evidence; selected neuroscience options inform existing curricula rather than generating an artificial additional route. A nanoscale physics/instrumentation programme cannot be assembled because the workbook lacks mechanics/optics, molecular/statistical biophysics, soft matter, electronic measurement and nanofabrication progression. General image processing or mathematical models cannot be relabelled as these subjects. No third programme is manufactured.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both directly study molecular/cellular biology. The external module also incorporates physical-cell content not fully offered by UCR.
Both study biomolecule chemistry and biological biochemical function. The complete external structural-biology syllabus is not asserted as covered.

Both involve practical molecular/biochemical techniques; UCR DNA, proteins, bacteria and bioinformatics laboratory work provides a substantive experimental relationship rather than nanoscale biophysics.
The UCR course directly studies genetics, mutations, genetic testing and molecular pathology. This covers an important genetics/disease part; it does not reproduce all molecular genetics.
The current TER identifies Math 1 as the successor to Analysis 1. UCR calculus foundations, with vectors/matrices, supply the important introductory mathematical method.
The current TER identifies Math 3 as combining former Analysis 3 and Linear Algebra. UCR directly implements its linear-algebra part; the analysis part remains broader.
UCR implements numerical methods and differential-equation computation, supplying an important scientific-computation method; it does not claim the same biological project or complete external scope.

The current TER identifies Math 2 as the successor to Analysis 2. UCR multidimensional calculus/differential equations provide a substantive advanced-analysis relationship, without asserting identical syllabus.
